newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac sees further margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac sees further margin pressure.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp Ltd said on Monday that intense competition may put further pressure on lending margins.
It also said that full franking of dividends would be maintained in the foreseeable future.
"Looking forward, competition is expected to remain intense and this may lead to further pressure on interest margins," Westpac chairman John Uhrig told the company's annual general meeting.
Uhrig said that in such an environment, improved performance would depend increasingly on better efficiency and not interest income generation.

"This, combined with our active capital and balance sheet management and a continued focus on asset quality and risk management, will be the key to sustaining positive trends in shareholder returns to more appropriate levels," he said.

Banks in Australia have been facing intense pressure in the home loan market from non-bank lenders, who, funded by the wholesale money markets, have reduced mortgage interest rates, forcing the banks to follow.

Uhrig said securitisation was likely to be an increasing trend due to the growing availability of funds to invest in certain types of securitised assets, as a result of the shift in household savings towards pooled investment vehicles.

On dividend franking, Uhrig said: "Recognising the enhanced value of fully-franked dividendd for most of our shareholders, directors have reaffirmed their expectation that full franking will be maintained in the foreseeable future."
He said also Westpac's purchase of AMPAC Life from AMP Society in October 1996 would make a positive contriubtion to earnings this financial year.
Westpac reported a net profit of A$1.13 billion for the year to September 30, up from A$947 million the previous year.
